source.title: Lisburn Standard, 23 January 1920, p. 6: "Lisburn Urban Elections—Official Results Sheet", Central Ward (facsimile of the official results sheet), with "Mercer's analysis of the voting" on p. 8. Party labels of the elected: Northern Whig, 24 January 1920, p. 6, and Belfast News-Letter, 17 January 1920, p. 6; the official Unionist candidates: their advertisement in the Lisburn Standard, 9 January 1920, p. 8.
source.publisher: Lisburn Standard (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every count transcribed from the official results sheet and checked against the p. 8 account of Shaw's surplus: every count adds to the printed valid vote of 1,166, each result is the previous result plus the transfer, the quota is 1,166 / 7 + 1 = 167 as printed, and the order of election is the sheet's; Johnston's first count is 43 (not the 48 the newspaper's own OCR gives), as the totals require

note: Proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919; polled 15 January 1920. Counted 16 January 1920 by the returning officer, T. M. Wilson (town clerk). The ward returned 6 members. Donaghy and Griffith finished level on 157 after the tenth count, short of the quota, and both were elected as the two highest; Donaghy was placed fifth as he had more first preferences. The results sheets give surnames only; first names are from the Northern Whig's list of the elected. Candidates with no party label were not on the official Unionist list and no report seen gives their party.
